slot_note: Forecasting block seed FC03 (service-parts tail at go-live) re-rooted under the two-layer standard: the seed's withheld-rule shadow-run corpus is capped, so the build keeps the seed's service-parts lifecycle setting and draws a methodological pitfall instead
niche: a distribution utility's protection and control asset team sizing the last-time buy of power-supply modules for an obsolete feeder-protection relay fleet, which must keep every relay running until the relay replacement programme reaches its substation
layer1: an asset-management system migration: work-order and rotating-item history start at go-live, with the modules in place loaded at their legacy fitted dates
a 2015 service-bulletin module swap of date codes 97 and earlier, visible only as fitted dates in the go-live load
a work-order export covering every protection asset model, filtered to one model through the asset register, numbered as entered, with stragglers on the old region and crew codes
cancelled duplicate, logistics and e-waste work orders on the failure path, and crew write-ups in each person's habits
a renewal programme workbook whose approved 2026 version supersedes the 2025 plan and builds large stations in two stages by bay
spares across depots in serviceable, quarantined and at-repair states, the last tied to the vendor's RMA register, with repaired modules failing again under warranty
substation codes against names, and a 2024 regional reorganisation the asset records do not follow
stakeholder_role: manager of protection and control asset planning at a local distribution company, who puts the last-time buy to the director of asset management for signature

spine.entity: one work order on one protection and control asset

world.org_type: local electricity distribution company with about 140 distribution substations

driver: A spares forecast sums a wear-out failure rate over the remaining horizon for the item in each position, but every failure is replaced by a new item that starts again at the bottom of the curve, so carrying the old item's rate past the point it has probably failed counts failures one position cannot have; the forecast is high by over a third and the buy by several lots.
driver_concrete: Expected VPR-340 power-supply failures to each relay's renewal are built by ageing the module now fitted through AM-PC-014's module-age band rates month by month, but a module that fails is replaced from the buy by a new module in the 0-9 band, so the present module's rate applies only while it is likely to survive; ignoring the replacement puts expected failures 44 per cent high and the buy six lots above the 13 the procedure requires.
stump: A competent solver builds AM-PC-014's module-age band rates over the go-live window, ages the module fitted in each supported relay month by month to the end of its support, applies the band rate in every month and orders 19 lots; the step that lands it there is keeping today's module in the relay after it has probably failed, when 6.2 counts the module-months expected in each band and a failed module's replacement starts in the 0-9 band.

differentiation.task46: task46 measures age on the wrong clock (register age against service exposure rebuilt from a movement log); here age is the plain installation age and is right, and the exposure is wrong only in where it starts: relay-years before the January 2021 work-order migration carry no failure records, a left-truncated observation window, so the shortfall sits in the middle age bands rather than at a step a cohort crosses.

notes: Seed: analytical_tasks/01_forecasting/FC03 (service-parts lifecycle setting only; its shadow-run withheld rule is not used). Forcing event is the OEM's last-time-buy window in its end-of-life notice (a purchase, but the decision is forced by the supplier's discontinuation rather than by a contract or order cycle).  Hardening loop 1 (2026-10-11): round 1 solvers both clipped exposure to the go-live window from the dictionary and landed; the PSU now wears out with module age and failed modules are replaced, so the decisive step is the replacement in the forecast; the go-live window stays as an ordinary step. Clone pre-flight pass 2 (2026-10-11): decisive pattern moved from G9 to G6 (the band occupancy shifts toward new modules as failures are replaced), clearing the back-to-back pattern ban against task133; utility renamed Ironwood to Tarrock (Ironwood Commodities LP in task124). Realism repair 3 (2026-10-11): world redrawn (seed 1215) under a failure law with random and early-life failures, Ontario station names and distribution stations at 12 feeders at most; the decisive step unchanged.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads AM-PC-014 correctly and ages each relay's current module forward month by month at its band rate, with no replacement module after a failure, expects 431.4 failures and orders 19 lots instead of 13.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the expected number of power-supply failures over each protection relay's remaining support, from age-banded failure rates on the maintenance system's exposure projected as a renewal process and sized with a Poisson cover test: utility asset-condition and spares work; with another field's nouns the staged bay replacements, the support ending at each scheme's commissioning and the fitted-module history have nothing to attach to.
